title: Sentence Structure, Part 2
sourceNote: The auto-captions are heavily garbled; the sentences were reconstructed from context and the teacher's explanation.
objectives: I can recognise the pronouns ich, du and Sie
I can explain what verb conjugation is
I can use the endings -e, -st and -en
I can conjugate wohnen, kommen, heißen and sprechen with ich, du and Sie

grammar.title: Persons: ich, du, Sie
grammar.body: When you talk about **yourself** you use *ich* (first person). When you talk **to** someone you use the second person: **du** for a friend or child (informal) and **Sie** for a person you do not know well (formal). The pronoun *Sie* (you, formal) is always written with a capital S.

grammar.title: Conjugation and endings
grammar.body: The basic form of a verb is the **infinitive**, e.g. *wohnen*. In a sentence the verb is **conjugated**: it gets an ending that depends on the subject. For *ich* the ending is **-e**, for *du* it is **-st**, and for *Sie* it is **-en**. The *Sie* form is identical to the infinitive.

grammar.title: Special cases
grammar.body:
With **heißen** the stem already ends in an s-sound, so *du* only gets **-t**: *du heißt* (not *heißst*).

With **sprechen** the vowel also changes with *du*: *e* becomes *i*: *du sprichst*. It is an irregular verb; irregular verbs get their own lessons.

mistakes.why: The stem *heiß* already has an s-sound, so only *-t* is added.
*sprechen* is irregular: e becomes i with *du*.

mistakes.wrong: Sie kommst aus Wien. (talking to a stranger)

pronunciation.tip: Say *sch-p* at the start: *sprechen*, *sprichst*. The *ch* is soft, as in *ich*.

dialogues.title: Formal and informal: meeting someone new

lines.en: Good day! What is your name?

lines.de: Ich heiße Martin. Und wie heißen Sie?
lines.en: My name is Martin. And what is your name?

lines.de: Ich heiße Lara. Ich wohne in Paris.
lines.en: My name is Lara. I live in Paris.
Where do you come from? (B knows C, so informal)

lines.de: Ich komme aus Frankreich. Sprichst du Deutsch?
lines.en: I come from France. Do you speak German?

tip: Learn each verb with its three forms: ich -e, du -st, Sie -en. Say them aloud as a mini song.

comprehension.q: What ending does the verb take with *ich*?
What ending does the verb take with *du*?
What ending does the verb take with *Sie*?
comprehension.a: -en, the same as the infinitive (Sie wohnen).

comprehension.q: Why is it *du heißt* and not *du heißst*?
comprehension.a: The stem already ends in an s-sound, so only -t is added.
Sprechen is irregular: the vowel changes from e to i.

exercises.title: Match German and English
exercises.instructions: Match each German form with its English meaning.

summary: Pronouns replace nouns: ich (first person), du and Sie (second person).
The verb is conjugated according to the subject.
Endings: ich -e, du -st, Sie -en (the Sie form equals the infinitive).
Stems ending in an s-sound (heißen) take only -t with du: du heißt.
Irregular verbs such as sprechen change their vowel: du sprichst.
